title: Internet, networks, DNS, domain names
learningObjectives: Explain internet, networks, dns, domain names and apply it to accessible, reliable web development.

understand.concept: The internet is a network of interconnected networks that exchange data using agreed protocols. DNS translates human-readable domain names into network addresses. A domain name is a registered name that can point to services through DNS records.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding DNS helps diagnose why a site name may fail even when a server is available. Domain registration, DNS hosting, and web hosting are separate services.
understand.analogy: DNS is like a contacts directory that maps a familiar name to a network destination.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; web protocols, browser behaviour, and accessibility requirements follow formal standards and platform implementations.

explain.narrative: The code displays a hostname only; actual DNS resolution is performed by the operating system or network resolver, not by this JavaScript statement.

examples.code: const domain='learn.example.com';console.log('Browser resolves the hostname through DNS before connecting:',domain);
examples.explanation: The code displays a hostname only; actual DNS resolution is performed by the operating system or network resolver, not by this JavaScript statement.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the concept; some browser examples require a real served page and supported APIs.

practise.guidedTask: Trace the path from typing a domain into a browser through DNS resolution and the server connection. Identify what A, AAAA, and CNAME records represent.
practise.independentTask: Apply the concept to a small web page. Record the expected behaviour, how you tested it, and any limitations or fallbacks.
hints: Use browser developer tools to inspect actual behaviour.
Test with keyboard and different viewport sizes.
Keep core content available when enhancements are unsupported.
